Your new company  
 Our client is a rapidly scaling, purpose-led organisation with a commitment to supporting vulnerable communities across Australia. Having undergone significant transformation over the last 12 months, the organisation is now executing an ambitious national growth strategy that includes new service offerings, strategic acquisitions and major investments in technology, systems and workforce capability. With plans for substantial growth over the coming years, the business is building the infrastructure, leadership capability and people frameworks required to support its next phase of expansion. For an accomplished People & Culture leader, this is a rare opportunity to step into a business that has both the vision and momentum to achieve something extraordinary. 
   Your new role  
 As People & Culture Manager, you will be at the centre of an exciting growth and transformation journey. Reporting to a senior executive leader, you will lead the People & Culture function and will be responsible for building the systems, processes, and frameworks required to support sustainable growth. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 
 Leading people strategy across a multi-state workforce. 
 
 
 Supporting business growth, integration, and change initiatives. 
 
 
 Driving HR systems, automation, and process improvement initiatives. 
 
 
 Building scalable people frameworks to support growth. 
 
 
 Leading workforce planning, talent acquisition, onboarding, and retention. 
 
 
 Managing employee relations, investigations, performance, and industrial relations matters. 
 
 
 Ensuring compliance across the SCHADS Award, Fair Work, WHS, and legislative requirements. 
 
 
 Partnering with executive leaders to strengthen culture, capability, and performance. 
 
 
 Success in this role will come from your ability to deliver outcomes, create scalable solutions, and support long-term organisational growth. 
   
  What you'll need to succeed  
 You are an experienced People & Culture leader who thrives in environments of growth, change, and complexity. Commercially minded and highly accountable, you enjoy building systems, structures, and teams from the ground up. 
   
 
 
 10+ years' experience in senior HR leadership roles. 
 
 
 Experience leading HR systems and transformation initiatives. 
 
 
 Strong Employee Relations, Industrial Relations, and investigation capability. 
 
 
 Proven success building high-performing teams and developing leaders. 
 
 
 Strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation, Fair Work, NES, and ideally the SCHADS Award (desirable). 
 
 
 The ability to influence and partner with executive stakeholders. 
 
 
 Strong stakeholder engagement and change management skills. 
 
 
 A hands-on approach and willingness to roll up your sleeves. 
 
 
 Experience in community services, disability, healthcare, aged care, NFP, or another regulated environment is highly desirable. 
 
 
 A track record of success in fast-paced, high-growth organisations. 
 
 
 Most importantly, you're a go-getter who embraces ambiguity, adapts quickly, and takes ownership for delivering results. 
 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 Join an organisation at a defining stage of its journey and help shape the future of its people function. 
 
 
 Genuine influence over executive decision-making. 
 
 
 Exposure to large-scale growth, transformation, and integration projects. 
 
 
 Flexible hybrid working arrangements and a highly autonomous leadership role. 
 
 
 Significant career progression opportunities. 
 
 
 The opportunity to lead meaningful transformation across people, systems, and culture. 
 
 
 A platform to build scalable systems, frameworks, and high-performing teams. 
 
 
 The chance to make a real impact within an organisation supporting vulnerable communities across Australia. 
 
 
   What you need to do now     If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.   If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion on your career.    Please  click here  to apply.

- Remuneration: $80,000 excluding superannuation
- Ayr, North Queensland location

Top of the Crop Labour Hire require an Office Manager to join their team in North Queensland.

Position Purpose

The Office Manager is responsible for managing the day-to-day administrative operations of Top of the Crop Labour Hire’s office in Ayr. The position oversees office administration systems, records management, compliance documentation, resource coordination and administrative support functions required for the effective operation of the business.

Working closely with Management, clients, operational teams and employees, the Office Manager ensures administrative processes are efficient, accurate and compliant with company policies, employment obligations and operational requirements.

The role provides supervision and support to administrative staff, coordinates office resources and contributes to continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and service delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Office Management & Operational Coordination:
- Manage the daily operations of the Ayr office and oversee administrative activities.
- Develop, implement and maintain office administration systems, procedures and workflows.
- Maintain accurate business records, employee files and operational documentation.
- Manage office facilities, equipment, vehicles and administrative resources.
- Coordinate purchasing activities, supplier relationships and office service requirements.
- Maintain the company’s information management systems and ensure data accuracy.
- Prepare administrative reports and provide operational updates to management.
- Identify opportunities to improve office processes and administrative efficiency.

Workforce Administration Support:
- Coordinate administrative processes relating to employee onboarding, induction documentation and personnel records.
- Maintain workforce databases, visa records and employment documentation.
- Provide administrative support for timesheet processing, payroll preparation and workforce reporting.
- Liaise with operational teams, clients and employees regarding administrative matters.
- Support accommodation and transport administration arrangements where required.

Leadership & Team Management:
- Provide day-to-day supervision and coordination of Welfare Support Officers who assist with administrative processes, employee documentation and workforce support services.
- Allocate workloads, monitor performance and support staff development.
- Foster a professional, inclusive and collaborative workplace culture.
- Support management with workforce planning, training and succession planning initiatives.

Compliance & Risk Management:
- The role maintains administrative systems and documentation to support compliance with applicable employment, immigration and business requirements, including obligations associated with labour hire operations.
- Maintain workforce records, visa documentation and compliance reporting systems.
- Coordinate audits, inspections and compliance reviews, ensuring documentation is accurate and audit-ready.
- Support workplace health and safety initiatives and promote safe work practices.
- Identify operational risks and implement corrective actions where required.
- Maintain confidentiality and integrity of business and employee information.

Stakeholder Engagement:
- Build and maintain positive relationships with clients, accommodation providers, transport providers, government agencies, medical professionals and community organisations.
- Coordinate workforce support services and assist in resolving employee and operational issues.
- Support accommodation inspections, vehicle inspections and general workforce welfare activities.

Continuous Improvement:
- Review and improve administrative processes to enhance efficiency and service delivery.
- Contribute to organisational planning, workforce management initiatives and business improvement projects.
- Support the achievement of operational, compliance and workforce objectives.

Essential Selection Criteria:
- Demonstrated at least one-year experience in office management, operations management or a similar role.
- Proven experience leading and supervising staff.
- Strong organisational, administrative and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder relationship management skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
- High-level proficiency in Microsoft Office and workforce administration systems.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
- Current Australian Driver Licence.

Desirable Criteria:
- Experience working with PALM Scheme participants or culturally diverse workforces.
- Knowledge of labour hire operations, workforce compliance and employment legislation.
- Experience coordinating accommodation, transport and workforce logistics.
- Experience with payroll administration and workforce reporting systems.
- Experience using SharePoint or workforce management platforms.

Key Attributes:
- Strong leadership and people management capability.
- Professional, approachable and accountable.
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
- Solutions-focused, adaptable and resilient.
- Committed to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Other Requirements:
- Bachelor’s Degree
- Advanced experience with Microsoft products
- Current Australian Driver Licence.
- National Police Check (or ability to obtain).
- Willingness to work flexible hours to meet operational requirements.

Since 1981, Shadbolt Group has grown to become a leading cost-effective engineering solutions provider. We are proud of our professional performance on each and every project. Our aim is to build long term relationships with our clients based on trust, accountability and integrity. It is our dedication to quality that gives our clients a competitive advantage.

This goes hand in hand with our diligence and engineering excellence. From pipework projects to tank manufacturing, structural works, machine building or site work. Shadbolt Group is committed to providing prompt and precise delivery from our highly trained team of experts. The requirements of each client are always the focus of everything we do.

We are seeking qualified Pressure Welders to join our growing professional team. We seek reliable, team-oriented individuals with high integrity who will positively contribute to the company's success. We offer short-term contracts with above-award pay rates fully guaranteed under current workplace regulations.
Position available across our site and work locations in NSW, SA, WA and VIC.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Read and interpret project plans, engineering drawings, blueprints and other written instructions and diagrams to determine and perform appropriate welding techniques for the task at hand
Set up equipment and weld parts, using appropriate pressure welding equipment and methods
Examine welds for width of bead, penetration and precision, and performs necessary repairs or reworks
Weld and repair pressure vessels and pipes to relevant high-quality standards and ensure conformance with standard specifications
Fabricate metal components in accordance with supplied drawings and specifications
Conduct tests on welds to ensure there are no leaks in the pressurised systems
Conduct quality checks on completed work to ensure it meets standard specifications
Apply post-weld treatments to relieve stress and enhance the strength of the welded joints on pressure-containing equipment
Diagnose faults and perform operational maintenance on machines and equipment in order to restore full functionality and safety performance, maintaining a condition that does not compromise safety
Maintain tools and equipment to a professional standard
Keep the workstation clean and orderly to retain a safe and operational work environment
Clean and prepare metal surfaces for welding by flame cutting, heat cutting, gouging, bevelling, grinding or filing
Manage workflow, meet deadlines, and troubleshoot problems on a daily basis, in addition to fabrication duties

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Trade qualified
Minimum of three years of experience in this role or similar
Ability to work independently and in a team environment to complete large and complex projects
Critical thinking
Strong attention to detail and the ability to conduct quality checks on completed work
Precision skills
Strong communication and reporting skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Safety focus
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!

Salary: $49.00/hour, 38 hours per week + Super

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Better & Fairer Care. Always.

Become the UKG Capability Expert

Drive Workforce Excellence

Influence Continuous Improvement 

At St Vincent's, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As Australia's largest not-for-profit health and aged care provider, we are committed to delivering exceptional, compassionate care and improving health outcomes for communities across New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria.
 

Guided by our values of Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence, more than 30,000 employees come together each day to make a genuine difference. When you join St Vincent's, you'll become part of a purpose-driven organisation dedicated to shaping a better and fairer health and aged care system for all.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an experienced UKG Support Specialist - Training to play a pivotal role in building workforce capability and supporting one of Australia's largest healthcare organisations.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about workforce technology, user education and continuous improvement. You'll become the go-to expert for UKG system training, empowering managers and employees to confidently navigate workforce management processes while ensuring payroll accuracy, compliance and operational excellence.

Working closely with Payroll, HR and operational leaders, you'll deliver engaging training programs, develop practical learning resources and provide advanced system support that enhances the employee experience across St Vincent's.

What You'll Do

Deliver engaging UKG training sessions for managers, employees and new starters

Develop and maintain user guides, quick reference materials, FAQs and training documentation

Provide advanced support and guidance on UKG, including timecards, rosters, leave, approvals and payroll-related processes

Act as an escalation point for complex UKG enquiries and coach users to build confidence and self-sufficiency

Identify recurring issues and knowledge gaps, delivering targeted education to improve system capability

Promote consistent, compliant and best-practice use of UKG across the organisation

Support payroll accuracy by monitoring schedules, timecards and workforce management data

Contribute to system testing, process improvements and enhancements to training resources

Work collaboratively with Payroll, HR and key stakeholders to improve the user experience and system adoption

About You

You're an experienced workforce systems, payroll or systems support professional who enjoys helping others learn, solve problems and succeed.

Passionate about customer service, training and continuous improvement, you have the ability to translate complex system functionality into practical, easy-to-understand guidance that empowers users and builds confidence. You thrive on building strong stakeholder relationships, delivering engaging learning experiences and helping people get the very best from technology. With a proactive, solutions-focused mindset, you're motivated by improving processes, enhancing user capability and driving operational excellence.

Key Experience & Capability

Demonstrated experience supporting workforce management or payroll systems, ideally UKG-Kronos.

Experience designing and delivering system training, workshops or user education programs.

Strong understanding of rostering, time and attendance, payroll processes and workforce compliance.

Proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve complex system issues while coaching and empowering end users.

Excellent written communication skills with experience developing learning resources, user guides and process documentation.

Strong stakeholder engagement and customer service skills, with the ability to communicate confidently across all levels of the organisation.

Highly organised with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Experience supporting system testing, process improvement, change initiatives or workforce systems optimisation will be highly regarded.
 

Why St Vincent's?

Make a meaningful impact - Help empower thousands of employees and managers to confidently use one of our most critical workforce systems.

Work with purpose - Join a values-driven organisation guided by Compassion, Justice, Integrity and Excellence.

Share your expertise - Lead training initiatives that improve system capability, payroll accuracy and workforce outcomes across a national organisation.

Enjoy great benefits - Access salary packaging, wellbeing initiatives, employee discounts and a range of additional benefits.

Be part of something bigger - Join a collaborative team committed to service excellence, innovation and continuous improvement.

Ready to Make an Impact? Apply now and help shape the future of workforce capability at St Vincent's Health Australia.
 

If you're passionate about workforce technology, user enablement and delivering exceptional customer experiences, we'd love to hear from you.

Please note applications will be reviewed as they are received, and the role may close early if a suitable candidate is identified.
 

For more information, contact TalentHealthVIC@svha.org.au.

Equal Opportunity

At St Vincent's we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued and empowered to thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, abilities, gender identities and life experiences.

Our workforce reflects the communities we serve, and we believe diverse perspectives make us stronger.
